abstract_coverage_prose: A single provider metric compared as a team's own production against the corresponding same-metric concession of the opponent (an attack-vs-concession 'mirror' on one metric).
A single metric conditioned on ONE opponent-profile band (HIGH/MID/LOW) along ONE of the frozen profile axes, versus a subject baseline.
A single metric contrasted by the subject's home/away venue, versus a subject or venue baseline (a pure venue split).
A single metric's recent-window level contrasted with its long-run level (recent-vs-long-run deviation / form).
A team's production on one metric read directly against the corresponding opponent concession of that same metric (direct cross-entity same-metric).
A single metric read against its competition/league environment baseline.
Any single-dimensional profile/venue/competition split already expressible by the existing conditioning grammar (arity 0 or 1).
A single metric read over a deterministically-computed cohort of opponents similar to the fixture opponent (existing similarity comparator).
The two closed arity-2 interactions the grammar already supports: venue crossed with a single opponent-profile band, and same-competition crossed with a single opponent-profile band.
Simple deterministic salience ranking / selection over existing enumerated candidates (no new representational construct).

unsupported_structures.description: A joint relationship between two or more DISTINCT provider metrics (not a single metric's for/against mirror) that cannot be reduced to one metric with one conditioning band.
A conditioning intersection over TWO DISTINCT opponent-profile axes simultaneously (profile x profile), which the grammar excludes by design.
A threshold / piecewise / nonlinear relationship on a continuous observable (not the fixed HIGH/MID/LOW tercile banding).
A within-match state construction (e.g. half-level split, or conditioning on a prior scoreline/game-state) where the provider resolution actually supports it.
An asymmetric attack-vs-defence relationship across DIFFERENT metrics (subject's metric A vs opponent's metric B, A != B).
A sequencing / regime / trajectory construction over ordered prior matches beyond a simple recent-window mean.
